name: Pennsylvania
summary: Statutes: palegis.us serves Pa.C.S. and the Constitution per section by a constructible iFrame URL, readable only by the script route — WebFetch is refused (robots.txt 403 to it); Justia 2025 is the WebFetch fallback. Purdon's P.S. has no free official compilation: palegis.us files unconsolidated law by act year/number. Court rules and agency regulations: pacodeandbulletin.gov (Pa. Code and Bulletin) disallows all robots, so Cornell LII is the only automated text (quarterly, some stale rules); the Bulletin has no reachable source. Case law: pacourts.us has a plain-GET JSON opinion API (Supreme, Superior, Commonwealth, 1998–) and slip PDFs readable by both routes; allocatur orders are found by party name only; UJS docket sheets refuse automation (401).

citation_map.notes: Pa.C.S. URL mapping: section number = chapter*100 + sctn (5524 → chpt=55, sctn=24; 102 → chpt=1, sctn=2; 62A01 → chpt=62A, sctn=1); a decimal goes in subsctn (5524.1 → sctn=24&subsctn=1). Title 13 (UCC) needs div = the leading digit of the section (13 § 2725 → div=2; § 9102 → div=9); other titles take div=00. (verified for 15, 18, 20, 23, 42, 75). Title 0 = Constitution (chpt = article, sctn = section). P.S. (Purdon's) is West's unofficial compilation of unconsolidated acts: a P.S. title/section does NOT map to a free URL; palegis.us files unconsolidated law by act year + act number (UTPCPL = Act 387 of 1968 = 73 P.S. § 201-1 et seq.), and the act text carries no P.S. numbers. Resolve the act from the citing text (courts usually give 'Act of Dec. 17, 1968, P.L. 1224, No. 387') or from law_aliases; P.S. section hyphens (201-2) are part of the section, not a range. '§§ 2501-2502' in a Pa.C.S. cite is a range: the regex takes 2501. Bare 'Vehicle Code', 'Judicial Code', 'Crimes Code' are shared with other jurisdictions (and the federal Judicial Code) — the prose pattern requires 'Pennsylvania'; bare 'Rule 1925(b)' or 'Rule 600' must not route here without Pa.R.*. Court rules are Pa. Code titles: Pa.R.C.P. = 231, Pa.R.A.P. = 210, Pa.R.Crim.P. = 234, Pa.R.E. = 225, Pa.R.J.C.P. = 237 (see law_aliases). Citability: Pa.R.A.P. 126(b) — non-precedential Superior Court memoranda filed after May 1, 2019 may be cited for persuasive value (verified on LII). Commonwealth Court unreported opinions filed after Jan. 15, 2008 are citable for persuasive value under its IOP § 414 (from memory, unverified). Docket codes: Superior EDA/MDA/WDA (pre-~2003 'PGH', 'PHL', 'HBG' and 2-digit years); Supreme EAP/MAP/WAP (appeals), EAL/MAL/WAL (allocatur petitions), EM/MM/WM (misc.); Commonwealth C.D./M.D. 'PA Super N' numbers appear on precedential Superior slip opinions only; the pacourts API cannot be searched by it — search by caption/docket. Official reporters Pa. Super. and Pa. Cmwlth. ceased in the late 1990s (from memory); modern cites are to A.3d. CourtListener ids pa / pasuperct / pacommwct are from memory, unverified.

access.pattern_rules: chapter = section // 100 and sctn = section % 100, both unpadded (5524 → chpt=55&sctn=24; 102 → chpt=1&sctn=2; 2502 → chpt=25&sctn=2); alphanumeric chapters keep their letters (62A01 → chpt=62A&sctn=1); decimal part → subsctn (5524.1 → subsctn=1), else subsctn=0. div=00. for every title except 13 (UCC), where div = the section's leading digit (13 § 2725 → div=2). ttl unpadded (ttl=0 for the Constitution). Without iFrame=true the page is a 1.6K nav shell whose text loads by script — always include iFrame=true. Omit sctn to get the whole chapter (42 ch. 55 = 81K chars). Whole title: /statutes/consolidated/view-statute?txtType={HTM|PDF|DOC}&ttl={title}. Unknown combinations return a 'could not be found' page, not a 404.
access.navigation: Index lists titles with History/HTML/PDF/Word links; it shows no section ranges. Construct the iFrame URL directly; history?ttl_id={title} lists amending acts.
access.read_via: script route only (fetch_doc.py). WebFetch is refused (ROBOTS_DISALLOWED) because robots.txt returns 403 to it.

sources.title: Unified Judicial System of Pennsylvania — Court Opinions and Postings
sources.official_status_evidence: Slip opinions with slip pagination; official/West reporter citations (A.3d) are not printed on them.
sources.coverage: Supreme Court, Superior Court and Commonwealth Court postings from 1998 (API year=1998: 137 / 142 / 187 items) to today. Includes opinions, memoranda, judgment orders, per curiam orders, allocatur dispositions, rule orders, judgment lists.

access.pattern_rules: Plain GET JSON (verified by script and WebFetch). court = Supreme | Superior | Commonwealth. Use either month+year (month may be empty for a whole year) or startDate/endDate. captionText is a substring match on the caption, which embeds the docket ('Com. v. Ly, C.\r\nNo. 1996 EDA 2025') — so captionText='1996 EDA 2025' finds a docket; first names are abbreviated (captionText=Cuong → 0). courtDocketNumber is ignored. Other params: authorName, keywords, publicationType, sortDirection; postTypes codes seen: mo (majority), paa (allocatur), pco, Memorandum, Opinion, Judgment Order. 20 items per page (TotalPages). Each item's Postings[].FileName → https://www.pacourts.us/assets/opinions/{Supreme|Superior|Commonwealth}/out/{FileName} (URL-encode spaces).
access.navigation: Court listing pages (/courts/{supreme|superior|commonwealth}-court/court-opinions) show recent postings with PDF links; the search form is JavaScript that calls the GET API above.

automation.notes: RSS: /Rss/Opinions/{Supreme|Superior|Commonwealth}/. PDFs read in full by both routes (29-page opinion complete in WebFetch).

hazards: slip pagination only — no A.3d page numbers
caption abbreviations (first initials, 'FCB' for First Commonwealth Bank) defeat party-name search
courtDocketNumber API parameter ignored
file names carry opaque numeric suffixes — take them from the API, never construct

script_candidates.why: Public GET JSON API /api/opinion (court, month/year or date range, captionText incl. docket, postTypes, paging) covering 1998–present for all three appellate courts, plus RSS per court; a script can resolve (court, docket, date) → PDF deterministically and find allocatur orders.

Deterministic per-section iFrame URLs (ttl/div/chpt/sctn/subsctn) and per-title HTM/PDF/DOC downloads; a script can serve exact text while WebFetch is robots-blocked, and can build a section index from whole-title HTML.
